Belarusian

[edit]
Belarusian Wikipedia has an article on:
ключ
Wikipedia be

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *kľučь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kljaukjas, from Proto-Indo-European *klewk-yo-s, from *kle(h₂)uk-, an extended form of *(s)kleh₂w- (“hook, key, peg”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [klʲut͡ʂ]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

ключ • (ključ) m inan (genitive ключа́, nominative plural ключы́, genitive plural ключо́ў)

  1. key
  2. wrench, spanner, screw wrench
  3. clue, key
  4. (music) clef, key
  5. radical (in Chinese characters)

Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
ключ
Wikipedia bg

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Church Slavonic ключь (ključĭ), from Proto-Slavic *kľučь.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [klʲu̟t͡ʃ]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ut͡ʃ

Noun

[edit]

ключ • (ključ) m (relational adjective клю́чов, diminutive ключе́ or ключе́нце)

  1. key (metal device used for locking, unlocking, or winding mechanisms)
    Вълчан си влезе в стаята, вратата се хлопна зад него и ключът два пъти се завъртя отвътре.
    Vǎlčan si vleze v stajata, vratata se hlopna zad nego i ključǎt dva pǎti se zavǎrtja otvǎtre.
    Valchan entered the room, the door slammed behind him, and the key turned twice from the inside.
  2. switch (mechanism in an electrical installation)
    Synonym: прекъсва́ч (prekǎsváč)
    Щракна електрически ключ и в краката на нощния посетител легна ивица светлина.
    Štrakna električeski ključ i v krakata na noštnija posetitel legna ivica svetlina.
    An electrical switch clicked, and a strip of light lay at the feet of the night visitor.
  3. wrench, spanner (tool for nuts, bolts, and screw, as well as tuning peg for musical instruments)
    га́ечен ключ
    gáečen ključ
    spanner, wrench
    фре́нски ключ
    frénski ključ
    adjustable wrench, monkey wrench
  4. (figuratively) key, clue (cipher, solution to a puzzle, riddle, strategic location, or figurative means of understanding)
    ключ към сърце́то
    ključ kǎm sǎrcéto
    key to the heart
    Трябва да им занеса и ключа на шифъра.
    Trjabva da im zanesa i ključa na šifǎra.
    I need to bring them the cipher's key as well.
  5. (music) clef
    но́тен ключ
    nóten ključ
    clef
    виоли́нов ключ
    violínov ključ
    treble clef
  6. (architecture) keystone

(dialectal) knot; stitch; joint (connecting bones)

  1. !(obsolete or dialectal) rolling boil, bubbling (of boiling water)
    Когато се изгубваше ключът, той пак възвиваше веригата и котелът пак завираше с ключ.
    Kogato se izgubvaše ključǎt, toj pak vǎzvivaše verigata i kotelǎt pak zaviraše s ključ.
    When the boil died down, he would pull up the chain again and the cauldron would come back to a rolling boil.
  2. (obsolete or dialectal) spring, geyser
    Synonym: и́звор (ízvor)
    От ледяната ѝ земя извират много горещи ключове.
    Ot ledjanata ì zemja izvirat mnogo gorešti ključove.
    Many hot springs emerge from its icy earth.

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak kľúč, from Proto-Slavic *kľučь. Cognates include Carpathian Rusyn ключ (ključ) and Slovak kľúč.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈkʎut͡ʃ]
  • Rhymes: -ut͡ʃ
  • Hyphenation: ключ

Noun

[edit]

ключ (ključ) m inan (diminutive ключик, relational adjective ключни)

  1. key
  2. wrench, spanner
    Synonym: французки ключ (francuzki ključ)
  3. (figurative) key (a crucial requirement or component)
  4. (education) key (any collection of solutions, explanations, or summaries)
    Synonym: ришенє (rišenje)
  5. key (small guide explaining symbols or terminology, especially the legend on a map or chart)
  6. (music) clef
    гушльов ключ ― hušlʹov ključ ― treble clef (literally, “violin clef”)
  7. source, wellspring
    Synonym: жридло (žridlo)

Russian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • ключъ (ključ) — pre-1918 spelling

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [klʲʉt͡ɕ]
  • Audio:(file)

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kľučь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kljaukjas, from Proto-Indo-European *klewk-yo-s, from *kle(h₂)uk-, an extended form of *(s)kleh₂w- (“hook, key, peg”), whence English clef and close.

Noun

[edit]

ключ • (ključ) m inan (genitive ключа́, nominative plural ключи́, genitive plural ключе́й, relational adjective ключево́й or клю́чный, diminutive клю́чик)

  1. key
  2. wrench, spanner, screw wrench
  3. clue, key
  4. (music) clef, key
  5. radical (in Chinese characters)
  6. (figuratively, usually with в (v)) way, vein (about the tone, character or manner of something)
    в том же ключе́ ― v tom že ključé ― in the same vein / along the same lines
    в э́том ключе́ ― v étom ključé ― in this/that vein/regard/context/way/manner
